subject: RegEdge Health — Private/VPC deployment criteria & next actions
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Lopez <carmen.lopez@regedgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — private hosting requirements (recap + next steps)

Thanks for the call this morning, Carmen — appreciate you walking us through the RegEdge stack. Below is a concise recap so we’re all aligned, plus proposed next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and we’ll adjust.

Recap (pain points & context)
- Regulated PHI workloads: no PHI may leave RegEdge-controlled network; auditability and key custody are hard requirements.
- Current infra: on-prem Kubernetes clusters in two colo sites (primary + DR), strict egress rules, limited outbound IP allowlist, bastion-only SSH for ops.
- Existing KMS: HashiCorp Vault-backed keys (HSM module) managed by security team.
- Pain: inference latency for mission-critical workflows, plus current vendor lock and opaque telemetry leading to compliance risk.

Success criteria (what will make a project successful)
- All inference-hosted compute must be reachable only within RegEdge VPC/colo (no raw model data egress).
- Support for customer-managed keys (Vault BYOK/HSM integration).
- Audit logs retained for >=90 days and accessible to RegEdge security team.
- Deployment must be supportable in air-gapped/offline mode or via a minimal connector pattern that respects egress allowlist.
- Latency target: 200ms p95 for typical 512-token requests for the triage model; throughput to handle ~30 qps burst.

Immediate asks for next step prep
- RegEdge to share: network topology (high-level), egress allowlist policy, and a non-sensitive sample of traffic patterns (QPS, typical token lengths).
- We will send: a short SOC2 evidence checklist, redwood network sample policy, and a proposed technical agenda for a deep-dive session.

Proposed next steps and timeline
1) Technical deep-dive with RegEdge security + infra (60–75m). Goal: validate connector architecture and confirm Vault keyflow. Proposed dates: Wed 2027-03-24 or Thu 2027-03-25 morning PT.
2) Exchange of artifacts (you send topology + allowlist; we send SOC2 evidence request & sample network policy).
3) If items align, follow with a scoped pilot SOW (6–8 weeks) and a procurement estimate to support Dedicated/Private deployment.

Attachments: regedge-infra-constraints.txt (please confirm), soc2-evidence-request.xlsx (we’ll send a sanitized template), redwood-network-sample-policy.yaml (sample).

Please confirm attendees for the deep-dive and which date/time works best. Thanks again — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0121
From: Carmen Lopez <carmen.lopez@regedgehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: it-security@regedgehealth.com, procurement@regedgehealth.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — private hosting requirements (recap + next steps)

Thanks, Priyom — solid recap. A couple clarifications from our side that matter for the deep-dive:

- Environment: this is primarily an on-prem, air-gapped deployment in our two colocation facilities. There is no general outbound internet access; we can allow egress only to a short list of IPs via firewall (we’ll provide).
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault with an HSM-backed keymaster. Keys are rotated quarterly and must remain under our control.
- Network ops: we will not run third-party containers that require unapproved upstream downloads during onboarding — any agent or runtime needs to be deliverable as signed artifacts.
- Logging: security requires immutable access + audit logs retained for 90 days and exportable to our Splunk instance.
- Timeline: procurement is targeting late Q2 (internal deadline 2027-06-30).

I attached a brief constraints file (regedge-infra-constraints.txt) that lists the approved egress pattern and the bastion/maintenance processes. I’ll ask our infra lead (cc’d IT security) to join the deep-dive if we schedule next week.

Carmen Lopez
Head of Infrastructure, RegEdge Health
carmen.lopez@regedgehealth.com

Hi Carmen / team — Marissa here (Solutions Lead). Thanks for the detailed constraints file, Carmen — super helpful. A few practical notes on what Redwood can offer and concrete next actions: 

What we can support today (high-level)
- Private connector model: a lightweight, signed connector that runs inside your network and communicates with Redwood control plane over a restricted set of allowed IPs/ports. For strictly air-gapped customers we offer an \"offline agent\" cadence where artifacts (models, runtime images) are signed and delivered via secure transfer — no direct internet pull required.
- KMS integration: we support Vault BYOK flows and can integrate via PKCS#11 or REST-backed keywrap depending on your Vault setup. HSM-backed keys are supported in our private deployment pattern.
- Logging & retention: we can export structured audit logs to your Splunk endpoint and retain a copy locally for the 90-day requirement.

Proposed immediate technical agenda (deep-dive)
- 10m: Introductions & objectives
- 25m: Network topology walkthrough and egress policy validation
- 25m: KMS keyflow (Vault) and signing/rotation expectations
- 15m: Offline agent delivery model & integrity checks
- 10m: Open questions / next steps

Attachments included: redwood-network-sample-policy.yaml (sample firewall rules + required outbound IPs), soc2-evidence-request.xlsx (short list of artifacts the security team typically requests), proposed-map.pdf (quick mapping of connector vs offline-agent tradeoffs).

Availability: Wed 2027-03-24 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2027-03-25 09:00–11:00 PT both work for our infra/security engineers. Please tell us who from your security/infrastructure team will join.

Thanks — Marissa
